newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate at 10.390 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate at 10.390 pct.

text.p: The Philippine 91-day treasury bill rate fell to 10.390 percent from the previous week's 10.392, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The other maturities, however, produced higher rates.
The 182-day rate rose to an average of 10.84 percent from 10.726, and the 364-day rate edged up to 11.489 from 11.396.
The auction generated 19.61 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 4.5 billion pesos were accepted.
Banks had expected higher T-bill after the Central Bank increased its overnight borrowing rate last Friday by 0.25 percentage point to 10.25 percent.
A Reuters poll of six banks had forecast the 91-day rate moving up to 10.53 percent, the 182-day rate to 10.96 percent, with the 364-day rate rising to 11.59 percent.
The market's ample liquidity tempered the increase in T-bill rates, traders said.
"And banks gave low rates to protect their positions," a dealer said. If T-bill rates had been higher, banks would have had difficulty selling their old, low-interest bills, the dealer said.

Central Bank managing director Amando Tetangco, a member of the government auction committee, told Reuters after the auction: "It (the auction results) indicated rates are moving towards stabilisation. Rates should stabilise at these levels."
This is the fourth consecutive week that T-bill rates had generally risen following a steep fall brought on by high liquidity and low inflation.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza reiterated that the recent adjustment in the overnight borrowing rate was a realignment with the domestic trend.
He said banks mostly preferred the 364-day bills which attracted almost half of the total tenders.
"The market has enough confidence on the long-term view of the Philippines," he said.
